levels.label: Universal identities
levels.description: Facts about the information carried by any hard label, before any criterion or solver is chosen.

levels.label: Score access
levels.description: How a score is obtained: exact densities, density ratios, or a calibrated classifier, and what each does to the information.

levels.label: Finite assignment
levels.description: Labels for a fixed weighted table of scores. The object is the partition itself, not a rule.

levels.label: Inductive rule from a sample
levels.description: A rule on score space fitted on a sample and applied to observations not yet seen.

levels.label: Sample to population
levels.description: Whether what is optimal on a sample converges to what is optimal under the population law.

levels.label: Population design
levels.description: The quantizer that is optimal under the score law itself, with no sample in the way.

levels.label: Information accounting
levels.description: How retained information is reported: efficiencies, spectra and direction-resolved diagnostics.

levels.label: Application
levels.description: Results stated for a specific use, such as template fits.

criteria.label: Criterion-independent
criteria.description: Results that hold for every matrix criterion, or that concern the information itself.

criteria.label: D-optimality
criteria.description: Maximises the determinant of the retained information on its informative subspace, weighing every parameter direction at once. The primary criterion of the library and of this research.

criteria.label: Profiled Ds-optimality
criteria.description: Maximises the determinant of the Schur complement for the parameters of interest after the nuisance parameters are profiled out. The second primary criterion; it lacks the D geometry, which is where most of the boundary results live.

criteria.label: Normalised trace
criteria.description: Maximises the trace of the whitened retained information, which is the k-means objective in whitened score space. A control criterion.

criteria.label: A-optimality
criteria.description: Minimises the trace of the inverse information. A control criterion: studied to learn where D-style geometry stops.

criteria.label: E-optimality
criteria.description: Maximises the smallest eigenvalue. A control criterion: the finite geometry fails, which is why the library offers no E solver.

lanes.label: Criterion-independent
lanes.description: Results that hold for every criterion.

lanes.label: D
lanes.description: D-optimality: the determinant of the retained information.

lanes.label: Profiled Ds
lanes.description: Profiled Ds-optimality: the determinant after nuisance parameters are profiled out.

lanes.label: Trace, A, E
lanes.description: The control criteria: normalised trace, A and E.
